verdict: Invitation Homes took in $731M, up 6%, and net income rose to $159M — helped along by $136M of gains on homes it sold — while core rental profit per share grew 2.4%.

kpis.label: Same Store NOI growth
kpis.note: net operating income from homes owned a year+

segments.name: Rental revenues
segments.note: Rent from roughly 86,000 single-family homes — blended rents grew 3.0% on new leases and renewals.

segments.name: Other property income
segments.note: Fees and other income from the homes — things like pet fees, smart-home services and resident charges.

segments.name: Management fee revenues
segments.note: Fees for managing homes owned by joint ventures and other partners.

segments.name: Homebuilding revenues
segments.note: Selling newly built homes — a new revenue line for Invitation Homes in 2026.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of the houses over their lives — a large non-cash charge that REIT investors add back in FFO.

opex.name: Property management expense
opex.note: The cost of leasing and managing the portfolio day to day.

opex.name: Casualty losses & impairment
opex.note: Storm and casualty losses and small write-downs on properties.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $92M, plus $44M of joint-venture losses, debt-extinguishment and other costs, were exactly offset by $136M of gains on homes sold in the quarter — net other items of $0M.

takeaways.title: Core profit per share inched up
takeaways.text: Core FFO per share rose 2.4% to $0.48 — helped by buybacks shrinking the share count — and full-year guidance midpoint was raised to $1.96.

takeaways.title: Home sales padded the profit
takeaways.text: Net income of $159M includes $136M of gains on homes sold. FFO, which strips those gains out, was $212M — down from $274M a year ago.

takeaways.title: Buybacks are the strategy
takeaways.text: Invitation Homes has repurchased nearly $1B of stock since December 2025, funded by home sales, and the board just authorized another $500M.

oneTimers: A $136M gain on sale of property (versus $46M a year ago) is included in net income; REIT yardstick FFO removes it.
footerNote: REIT presentation: cost of revenue combines property operating and maintenance ($264M) and homebuilding cost of sales ($32M). As a REIT, Invitation Homes distributes its income to shareholders as dividends instead of paying corporate income tax, so there is no tax line; the $136M gain on sales is stated net of tax in the release. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $158M.
